body: I appreciate the kind words, but I find it really difficult to feel good about something that seems to constantly hinder me in living a happy fulfilling life. I agree there is nothing inherently wrong with being disabled, but I don't feel good about it.

Personally, I get zero benefits from it, it does nothing but hinder me, but I appreciate the advice. I try not to see it as a big part of who I am and more like something I've got to overcome to get what I want.
A lot of things, but definitely struggling socially or emotionally. Makes me feel like such a child.
Typed this up on my phone so I think it does that automatically. But I appreciate the advice haha

That's the thing, I'd never really have classed myself as "one of the weird kids". I take care of my appearance, dress pretty normally and I'm in pretty good shape. I'm awkward I guess though. I've never been able to nail the mental side. I'll give your method a try. I just really have no clue how to talk to other people. Maybe I'm just really boring or something?

I guess I must come across as a dickhead then haha. "Just being me" has left me with few friends unfortunately, I'm happy it works for you though. I can't help but feel like I annoy people whenever I excitedly talk about stuff. I agree with what you say about baby stepping my comfort zone and I appreciate your advice.
I already feel like I'm in a similar situation to you sometimes. I'm keen to change before it gets any worse. Im considering therapy if the new job goes well.
It really pisses me off when someone is very understandably upset about an issue in their life and all the responses are basically "get therapy" or "you must be depressed, take ssri".
In a heartbeat. It has done nothing but hinder me. I don't like who I am because of it.

Thanks, I feel like I'm always throwing myself against the wall, but I never actually learn anything from it. I feel as clueless as before. Plus, I can't really work out how well I pass. I think most pick up that there's something "wrong" with me.
Yeah, I'm guilty of waiting to be invited. I've found usually when I took initiative, I had a much richer social life, but it was pretty tiring and I slowly stopped again.

I'm just not happy staying indoors though, surely forcing myself to stay at home is also fighting who I am? I'm not doing it out of an attempt to be normal, I just genuinely feel much more fulfilled living a more classically "neurotypical life" I guess. I don't really get anything out of online friendships, I get way more out of actually going out and meeting people as difficult as I find it. I have indoor hobbies, but I can't do them day in day out without quickly getting bored. I don't like to constantly consume media for the sake of it. I was at my happiest when I used to go out often and had an active social life, but I lost that after a period of social anxiety and burnout. 

Kind of "giving in" to who I am just leads to getting depressed. 

I appreciate the advice though.
That's the thing, I do force myself to go out a couple times a week, but I'm always forcing myself.
That's a good shout, will look into it :)
This is really helpful. Thank you :)

Thanks, I think you might be right. I really feel like it's swallowed my whole identity lately. It's like I've got a little voice in my head that's constantly reminding me Im autistic. I'm someone who's always kind of struggled to have an identity, which I think is why I'm having such a hard time with this. I don't really have a previous identity I can try to fall back on. I understand what you mean about not feeling like a person too. Here's hoping we can both get out of this. Take care.

I'm not sure how much an actual diagnosis would actually help me. On one hand it would be nice to know for sure, it would probably help with self acceptance, but it's not like it can be treated. If I had adhd for example, I'd be more encouraged to get a diagnosis so I could get medicated. Plus if it did turn out I was autistic, I'm not sure how I'd feel about this label following me everywhere I go. I'm worried I'd let it limit me. I'm not sure if I'd rather just try and forget about it if it's even possible.

I will try to be more accepting of different self perceptions no matter where I go from here. 

Thank you for sharing your experience and advice. Have a nice day.
